note: THE PAPERCLIP OPENS NOTHING — a regression THE-331 shipped GREEN. The founder, on AdminCommunity desktop: 'im clicking on the paperclip and nothing appears.' The menu was opening the whole time: it was in the DOM, focusable, and its rows answered a hit test. It was painted at opacity 0 in the document's top-left corner. THE CAUSE WAS THE TRIGGER'S REF, not a z-index and not a collision flip. AttachMenu shipped the trigger as render={<Button …/>}, and ui/button.tsx exports a PLAIN FUNCTION COMPONENT; under the React 18 this repo pins, a function component cannot receive a ref, and React says so out loud ('Function components cannot be given refs'). Menu.Positioner anchors to the trigger's DOM node, so with a null ref it never ran a measurement and stayed at its pre-measurement state: opacity 0, transform translate(0px, 0px), --anchor-width unset. Measured in a real Chromium, and proved both ways with controls: a bare trigger anchored at translate(69px, 713px); the same trigger behind <Button> did not move at all. The fix keeps the primitive's costume — DropdownMenuTrigger renders its own element wearing buttonVariants({variant:'ghost',size:'icon'}) — so Base UI holds the ref it needs. THIS TICKET OWNS ONE SOURCE FILE. firestore.rules, firestore.indexes.json, functions/ and src/app/layout.tsx are byte-identical and pinned as literal digests in this ticket's own suite, which shells out to nothing; all 43 installed primitives are byte-identical; no npm dependency, no token and no component was added.

entries.why: THE-337 owns this file. The trigger no longer uses `render={<Button …/>}`: Base UI's Menu.Trigger renders its OWN element now and wears `buttonVariants({ variant: 'ghost', size: 'icon' })` plus the same `min-h-11 sm:min-h-0` tap target, so the paperclip is visually unchanged while Base UI finally holds the DOM node it anchors the positioner to. That single change is the whole regression fix and it is measured, not argued: the new suite reads the POSITIONER's own inline style off the shipped component and fails if it is still `opacity: 0; transform: translate(0px, 0px)` with `--anchor-width` unset. 🔴 REJECTED, and measured to fail: wrapping Button in a local React.forwardRef — the ref then reaches Button, which still drops it, and the positioner stayed transparent. The one true fix is React.forwardRef INSIDE ui/button.tsx, which would repair every anchored `render={<Button/>}` in the repo; that file is byte-frozen by nine other tickets' digest guards with no append point, so it is REPORTED rather than amended and the fix is made at this call site. `popover` was rejected as the primitive: it has no submenu, and the four category flyouts are the surface. ⚠️ ALSO RECORDED HERE: the `z-[110]` on DropdownMenuContent is INERT and is deliberately left in place. That className styles the Base UI POPUP; the POSITIONER above it is hardcoded `isolate z-50` in ui/dropdown-menu.tsx, and `isolation: isolate` opens a stacking context, so the popup's 110 is painted at the positioner's 50. A hit test against a layer at the nav's own z-[100] found the open menu covered at every sampled pixel, at all six widths. It does not bite today — the composer sits above the nav, Base UI collision-flips the menu upward and the two never intersect, zero occluded pixels at 380/768/1024/1280/1440/1920 — and 110 remains the RIGHT NUMBER (above the nav's 100 and the dialog primitives' 101/102, below the settings dialog's 200 and the modals' 300). Only the element it lands on is wrong, and correcting that needs one line in the frozen primitive. Nothing else moved: the four record types and their labels (docs/contacts/campaigns→'Fundraising'/forms), the shared AttachTypeIcon, `searchScope="deep"`, `virtualize={false}` and the load-on-first-open rule are all unchanged and are each measured by the new suite.
